predecessors.text: Bengkulu province, the west-Sumatra coast round Fort Marlborough; the pages give no boundary for the British holdings, so the modern province (20,182 km2 on the page) stands as an upper bound

successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: Bengkulu province, the west-Sumatra coast round Fort Marlborough; the pages give no boundary for the British holdings, so the modern province (20,182 km2 on the page) stands as an upper bound

ledger.x: 1685: the English East India Company settles at Bengkulu.
1 March 1825: the company's Bencoolen ends with the transfer to the Netherlands (treaty signed 17 March 1824; 'All transfers of property and establishments were to take place on 1 March 1825').

certainty.note: The company held forts and pepper districts on the coast; no page gives a boundary, and the shape is the modern province.
